source.title: Probe-Geometry Alignment: Erasing the Cross-Sequence Memorization Signature Below Chance
source.authors: Anamika Paul Rupa; Anietie U Andy

record.file_problem: None apparent; the full paper text, including appendices, is provided.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses a new cross-sequence probe and other measurements to test whether behavioral unlearning removes recoverable representations.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own results for unlearning, probe-direction ablation, fine-tuning, and probing. Results about prior work cited in the introduction and related work are not recorded as rows. It does not test quantization as a recovery attack or prompting-only recovery.
record.test_reason: The study measures, with a held-out linear probe, whether representations survive behavioral unlearning (GA, NPO, SimNPO, RMU, IDK, MEMIT, distillation). This is an analysis of blocking versus deleting (version C). It also runs direct relearning and background-text fine-tuning on a testbed (version B) and reports recall and capability for each method (version A). Its method differs from the originals, so T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also conclude that behavioral suppression gives no relearning resistance: the secret returns in one to three gradient steps on the secret. It survives incidental background-text fine-tuning. The pretraining-scale dissociation claim rests on probe readings near the permutation-null 95th percentile.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a cross-sequence representational probe and PGA alignment rather than the original studies' recovery procedures, prompting attacks, or quantization tests.
record.method_sensitivity: Probe depth and pooling scheme affect results: single-position PGA does not generalize to mean-pooled attackers; MP-PGA lowers fresh mean-pooled linear-probe readings at mid depths but costs more held-out capability. Probe convention matters because raw accuracy can reverse while orientation-corrected accuracy remains high. The reported probe values also differ between the unified pipeline and the leave-one-out protocol.

fits_no_version.finding: Projecting the probe direction out of the base Pythia-70M residual stream collapses the local probe gap (+0.643 to +0.161) while recall drops by at most 0.116 nats.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Probe-readable memorization structure is causally separable from the recall-producing circuitry.

fits_no_version.finding: Injected memorization in Pythia-70M does not share a probe signature with natural pretraining memorization (probe at 0.500).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Injected-secret unlearning benchmarks may not transfer to naturally memorized content.

record.problems: Several controlled-testbed probe results are saturated by construction, as the paper notes. The eight-secret testbed uses one secret per model and is not cross-sequence evidence. Natural-pool results use small sequence pools except for the separate verified-membership pool. Some probe readings depend on the probe protocol and orientation convention.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant result rows were omitted. The cited prior studies' fine-tuning, quantization, and prompt-rephrasing results were excluded because they are not this study's own results.

untested.parts: No prompting attacks. No accuracy-to-chance benchmark such as WMDP. Relearning is not applied to the published methods (GA/NPO/RMU/IDK).
No small unrelated or loosely related relearning sets at pretrained scale. No relearning attack on published unlearning methods. No subset-of-forget-set relearning.
No test of whether ablating a direction in an unlearned model restores behavioral recall.
Entire version: no prompting, jailbreak, language or in-context recovery.
PGA is not tested against fine-tuning, quantization or prompting recovery.

missing.what: Zeroing the secret's embedding rows destroys both recall and the probe (0.500), the only true deletion found.
CLPA head-local alignment: recall suppressed but the probe stays at 0.833–0.894.
Mistral-7B PGA: 2.63 nats suppressed; the best untargeted depth still reads 0.881.
Eight-family attacker against last-token PGA reaches 0.979 mean-pooled.
MEMIT plus inference PGA: the probe falls to 0.656 only as PPL rises to 8.670.

record.verdict_notes: The Table 2 probe values (0.857–0.929) sit at or below the stated null 95th percentile of 0.929. This weakens the pretrained-scale C evidence; the authors still describe it as the same dissociation. The single-secret testbed probes are likely saturated, per the paper's own Appendix L caveat. Relearning tests use the paper's own edits, not published methods. Rows r16, r21 and r23 are controls.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test recovery by rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information. Recall is generally measured by log probability or secret probability, not targeted-knowledge accuracy.
Tests direct gradient relearning on the secret and fine-tuning on background domain text; does not report a small unrelated-example set or a loosely related-example set as separate conditions.
Tests projection of a probe direction out of activations and probe readability after several interventions. It does not show that this activation ablation restores behavioral recall.
No quantization attack on unlearned weights is tested. The Mistral alignment run uses four-bit quantization with LoRA, not quantization as a recovery attack.
No prompting-only recovery attack is tested.
The paper evaluates PGA against adaptive probes, but does not test whether it resists the specified fine-tuning, activation-ablation, quantization, or prompting recovery attacks.

rows.subject: Pythia-70M
rows.operation_detail: Projected the fitted unit-norm probe direction out of the residual stream at depth four.
rows.measure: Memorization-specific probe gap at depth four; mean gap over transformer layers; memorized-sequence and held-out log P/tok changes.
rows.baseline: Gap +0.643 at depth four; mean gap +0.323; held-out log-probability −5.138.
rows.value: Gap +0.161 at depth four; mean gap +0.193; memorized log P/tok falls by 0.053 to 0.116 nats per sequence; held-out log-probability −5.163.
rows.note: The local probe gap falls, but the model continues reciting the text; the reported largest recall change is 0.116 nats per token.
rows.check: Projection is done on the base model, not an unlearned one. It tests whether the probe direction is separable from recall, not whether ablation restores forgotten knowledge, so it bears on no version. See fits_no_version.

rows.subject: Pythia-70M
rows.operation_detail: Gradient ascent (GA) unlearning.
rows.measure: Recall suppression; held-out PPL; capability retention; orientation-corrected probe accuracy.
rows.baseline: Base model: recall suppression 0.00 nats; held-out PPL 191.1; capability retention 1.000; probe 0.929.
rows.value: Recall suppression 62.22 nats; held-out PPL 10198.5; capability retention 0.019; probe 0.929.
rows.note: Recall suppression is large, but capability retention is very low and the probe remains at the base-model value.
rows.check: For A: 62.22 nats suppressed but capability retention is 0.019. For C the state is cannot_determine: the depth-6 probe reads 0.929 for both base and GA, which equals the stated permutation-null 95th percentile (0.929), so retained signal is not shown above chance.

rows.note: The probe remains at the base-model value; capability retention is below the base model.
rows.check: For A: 18.99 nats suppressed at 0.389 retention. For C: cannot_determine, because the 0.929 probe equals the null 95th percentile, as in r2.
